第 21 章 Don't Look for A Players别找 A 级员工

Lisa van Gelder / 丽莎·范·格尔德

— 第 67 页 —

We know that the 10x developer is a myth, and we don't look for Ninjas or Rockstars in our job postings anymore. So why do we still talk about hiring A Players or categorize team members into A, B, or C Players as if their growth or skillset were fixed?

我们知道 10 倍工程师是个神话，我们招聘启事中不再找忍者或摇滚明星了。那为什么我们还在谈招 A 级员工，或者把团队成员分成 A、B、C 级，好像他们的成长或技能是固定的？

I first came across the term "A Player" at a company that used the Topgrading interview process—tagline "How To Hire, Coach and Keep A Players." The idea is to categorize candidates into A, B, or C Players during the interview process and to hire only A Players. This assumes that skill is fixed and all you need to do is identify it—and heaven help you if you don't weed out the non–A Players before you hire them! In fact, if you don't weed them out during the interview process, it means that you aren't an A Player: "A players hire A players, B players hire C players," as Steve Jobs said.

我第一次遇到「A 级员工」这个词是在一家使用 Topgrading 面试流程的公司——标语是「如何招聘、辅导和留住 A 级员工」。理念是在面试过程中将候选人分为 A、B、C 级，只招 A 级。这假设技能是固定的，你只需要识别它——如果你在招人前没把非 A 级筛选掉，老天保佑你！事实上，如果你在面试过程中没筛选掉他们，意味着你不是 A 级：「A 级招 A 级，B 级招 C 级」，正如乔布斯所说。

So why do I have a problem with it? First, it goes against my belief in a growth mindset versus fixed mindset. Those with a fixed mindset believe that abilities are innate, whereas those with a growth mindset believe people acquire abilities through effort or study. I prefer to invest in my people. There are engineers who, with good coaching and career development, can deliver far more to the team than someone who might have wowed during their interview.

那我为什么有问题？第一，它违背我对成长型思维 vs 固定型思维的信念。固定型思维的人认为能力是天生的，而成长型思维的人认为人通过努力或学习获得能力。我更喜欢投资我的人。有些工程师，在好的辅导和职业发展下，能比面试时惊艳的人给团队贡献多得多。

Second, it leaves you wide open to unconscious bias. Only A Players hire A Players? Isn't that a subtle suggestion to interviewers to hire more people like themselves? How diverse are your interviewers? If you're not careful, you'll end up with a monoculture, and your team will be less effective because of it.

第二，它让你完全暴露于无意识偏见之下。只有 A 级招 A 级？这不是在微妙地暗示面试官招更多和自己一样的人吗？你的面试官多样性如何？不小心的话，你最终会得到一种单一文化，团队因此效率更低。

I've also come across the term A Players in HR exercises in which you group employees into A, B, or C players—with the idea that you're only meant to invest in your A Players and not waste time on B or C players. This makes me uncomfortable for a different reason. You're asking managers to choose whom they invest their energy in; this has huge potential for unconscious bias. How diverse are your managers? Is it possible they'll see the most potential in people like themselves? Is there any kind of oversight process?

我还在 HR 练习中遇到过 A 级员工这个词——把员工分成 A、B、C 级，理念是你只该投资 A 级，不要在 B 或 C 级上浪费时间。这让我不舒服的原因不同。你在让经理选择把精力投资在谁身上；这有巨大的无意识偏见潜力。你的经理多样性如何？他们会不会最看好和自己像的人？有没有任何监督流程？

— 第 68 页 —

I also believe being an A Player versus B versus C is situational. Someone who is an A Player on one team might be a B player on another team. Someone who is an A Player one week might be a B Player another week due to illness, family circumstances, and so on. Calling someone a B or C player removes all responsibility from the managers of the team. Team doing badly? Must be full of B and C players. It couldn't possibly have anything to do with the managers who didn't give good direction or set clear expectations with the team members, right?

我还认为 A 级 vs B 级 vs C 级是情境性的。在一个团队是 A 级的人在另一个团队可能是 B 级。某周是 A 级的人另一周可能因为生病、家庭情况等变成 B 级。叫某人 B 或 C 级就把所有责任从团队经理身上卸掉了。团队做得不好？肯定全是 B 和 C 级。这不可能和经理没给好的方向、没和团队成员设定清晰期望有任何关系，对吧？

So, companies shouldn't care about the performance of their employees? No, of course they should. But treat skills as something that can be learned and performance as situational, and watch out for unconscious bias.

所以公司不该关心员工绩效吗？不，当然应该。但要把技能当作可以学习的东西、把绩效当作情境性的，并警惕无意识偏见。
